explanation: Searched Mathlib for any other declaration stating that coercion ℝ → EReal reflects ≤. `EReal.coe_le_coe_iff` occurs only as the theorem itself; the only related declarations are `EReal.coe_le_coe` (the `gcongr` alias for the forward direction only, not the iff), `EReal.coe_ennreal_le_coe_ennreal_iff` and `EReal.natCast_le_iff` (different sources/targets), the special cases `EReal.coe_nonneg`/`coe_nonpos`/`coe_pos`/`coe_neg'` (one side fixed at 0), and the order embedding `EReal.orderEmbedding` whose `map_rel_iff'` field is part of a definition rather than a named theorem. No declaration in the generic order hierarchy (e.g. `WithBot.coe_le_coe_iff`, `WithTop.coe_le_coe_iff`, `StrictMono.le_iff_le`) yields this statement in one or two lines without going through the library's own lemma `EReal.coe_strictMono` (itself a composition of two strict-monotonicity results), so no duplicate or single-declaration special case was found.
